subject: Re: Demo recap & procurement path for Acme Retail
messages:

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap & next steps (Redwood + Acme)

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and actionable next steps so we don’t lose momentum:

- Goal: Serve personalized product descriptions on homepage with <100ms tail latency, target 50k requests/day.
- Demo highlights: streaming responses, fallback to smaller model for spikes, per-route cost visibility.
- Commercial path options discussed: purchase order (PO) via finance, corporate card for pilot, or marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace) if you want SaaS billing.

Open items / asks from Acme:
1) Which buying channel do you prefer (PO / card / marketplace)?
2) Who on your procurement team I should loop in for contract/PO timelines?
3) Any mandatory security/redline items we should expect from legal?

I’ve attached a short procurement checklist that maps requirements to typical timelines. Hannah (cc) is our commercial ops lead — she’ll help with the PO vs card path and provide the checklist you can share with finance.

If useful, propose a 30-min working session with procurement this week — Tue/Wed morning PT works for our team.

Thanks,
Marissa

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Demo recap & next steps (Redwood + Acme)

Hi Marissa — great demo, thanks. A few clarifying notes from procurement side:

- For pilot under $25k, procurement prefers corporate card to avoid creating a new PO. For anything above, we need a PO and 30–45 day payment terms.
- Marketplace is attractive (simpler billing), but legal requires a review; timeline is typically 3–4 weeks for Marketplace onboarding.
- Our finance lead (Tom Ellis) is copied — Tom, can you confirm whether we have any internal threshold that would force a PO for a pilot?

Also, we have a standard security questionnaire — I can push it to you in the next email. Our key urgency: pilot by Sept 7th. If we need a PO and it takes 3 weeks, that may push us.

Thanks,
Lisa Nguyen
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Retail
Lisa.Nguyen@acme-retail.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acme-retail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap & next steps (Redwood + Acme)

Hi Lisa — appreciate the context and the pilot timeline. I wanted to lay out a recommended path depending on which buying channel you choose, so you can share with finance/legal quickly:

Option A — Corporate card (recommended for pilot <$25k):
- Timeline: sign SOW + card payment = 2–5 business days (internal approvals dependent).
- Docs needed: SOW + standard commercial terms (we can use our hosted hosted API agreement).
- Action: If Tom confirms card approval, Marissa will send SOW and call-to-action for payment.

Option B — PO + Net 30/45:
- Timeline: 10–20 business days (procurement + legal + finance routing).
- Docs needed: SOW + invoice remit + insurance and SOC 2 evidence (we’ll supply).
- Action: If you choose PO, we’ll need a PO contact and an example PO template to ensure fields map.

Option C — Marketplace (AWS/GCP) billing:
- Timeline: 3–4 weeks for onboarding + any legal review.
- Tradeoffs: Simplified billing but longer lead time.

To speed things up, I attached a one-page procurement checklist and a draft SOW with two purchase options (card pilot vs PO). If you want, we can do a 30-min working session tomorrow to align on which path keeps you to the Sept 7 pilot start date.

Attachments: Redwood_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx, SOW-draft-Acme-Redwood.pdf

Quick asks for Tom/procurement team:
- Can you confirm whether a pilot <$25k can be processed on a corporate card?
- If PO is required, please share the PO template and expected routing/approver names.

Ben and Soojin are on copy for billing and operations questions — they’ll help with remittance/payment fields and any insurance/SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Commercial Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
